the security of data is an important consideration when using mobile devices for electronic prescriptions.
the Bluetooth protocol is a suitable mechanism to transfer electronic prescriptions between mobile devices and is more suitable than the near field communication (nfc) protocol.
Bluetooth for Health is more amenable than NFC for the security of ePrescription data in transit on mobile devices.

the security of data transfer in the electronic transfer of ePrescriptions.
the security of electronic prescription data in transit.
the development of a mobile device application for the transfer of electronic prescription information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a viable solution to the security of data at rest and data in transit using mobile devices for the transfer of electronic prescription information.
Bluetooth is the preferred method of transferring data in transit for electronic prescriptions on mobile devices.
the use of mobile devices to transfer electronic prescriptions using Bluetooth is a viable solution for the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of Bluetooth for Health as a mechanism for the secure transfer of electronic prescriptions is viable, but requires further research into the security and interoperability aspects of Bluetooth for Health.
Bluetooth for Health is a viable solution to transfer electronic prescriptions between mobile devices.
the security of the electronic transfer of prescription information can be achieved using Bluetooth for Health.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Bluetooth is a more reliable, interoperable and secure mechanism than NFC for the transfer of electronic prescription data between mobile devices and is an important consideration for the future of electronic prescription transfer in Australia.
the use of Bluetooth as a data transfer solution for the electronic prescription transfer between a prescriber and a patient is a viable and cost-effective solution.
there is an alternative and more cost effective solution to the centralised exchange model for electronic prescription transfer.
